skip_reason: Not a sales or quoting call. This is an inbound service escalation from a customer whose move is already in progress: 'I've got some of your guys out here moving my department and one of them is pretty sick... I just wanted to kinda get some idea of what the rest of the move looks like with that.' No quote, pricing, estimate, or booking is discussed at any point. Nicole's entire role on the call is warm-transfer triage — she confirms which movers are on site ('Abraham and Ken, and you only had Abraham, no other movers?'), and then works to reach the operations manager the crew told the customer to ask for ('They said to call this number and to talk to garrison whoever that is at management'), placing the customer on hold twice while she does. The transcript also ends mid-transfer with the customer still on hold ('Thank you, stay on the line.'), so there is no resolution, no handoff language, and no close to evaluate even on the sections that might otherwise apply. Existing-customer logistics with no quoting — not gradeable against the sales scorecard.
top_strength: Not scored, but worth noting for the service side: Nicole did the two things that matter most on an in-progress-move escalation. She apologized without deflecting or blaming the crew — 'I really do apologize for the inconvenience it costs you' — and she asked permission before every hold rather than dropping the customer cold: 'Would it be okay if I will put you on hold while checking' and again 'would it be okay if I'll put you on hold again?' She also tried to verify the facts on the ground before escalating, pushing to confirm the crew count ('Abraham and Ken, and you only had Abraham, no other movers?'), and she correctly caught the customer's request for a specific manager and took ownership of routing it rather than telling him to call back. The customer stayed cooperative throughout — 'Yeah, yeah, that's great. Thank you' and 'Absolutely' — which is the right outcome for a caller with a sick mover slow-walking his office move.
coaching_note: No sales coaching applies — this call should be excluded from the rep's sales average. One service-side note if it is reviewed anyway: the crew-count confirmation looped three times ('you only have one mover... Abraham and Ken, and you only had Abraham, no other movers?') before the customer clarified 'No, they are both here and Abraham is trying to continue but he's definitely sick and moving real slow.' Reading the situation back once in plain terms would have been faster and would have landed better on a frustrated caller: 'So both Abraham and Kenneth are on site, but Abraham is sick and the pace has dropped — let me get Garrison on this and find out what we can do about the rest of the day.' That confirms the facts, names the actual problem the customer called about, and tells him what happens next before the first hold. Separately, this is a process flag rather than a rep issue: a customer with an active job was told by the crew to call the general sales line and ask for a manager by first name, and the rep had no direct path to that manager — she had to hold twice hunting for him. Worth checking whether there is a defined escalation route for mid-move crew problems.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and appropriately apologetic with permission asked before each hold, but the language stayed procedural and slightly stilted, with no real acknowledgment of the customer's underlying frustration about a slow, sick crew on his office move.
